rows.description: A child learns that saying I need help is a strength and picks who to ask, such as a teacher, elder or friend. Children who never ask may fear being judged and benefit from a safe culture.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A school-age child asks may I go or can I have it and learns that permission depends on safety, timing and trust. Clear reasons for a no help the child accept it.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child who commands peers may be leading, anxious, or copying adult tone. Adults can coach the child to swap commands for invitations, such as how about we.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A school-age child suggests how to play a game or advises a friend on a problem. Advice that is not asked for can feel bossy, so asking would you like ideas is kinder.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child asks for privacy in the bathroom, with a diary or during a change of clothes. Adults honour reasonable privacy and explain safety limits, such as adults knowing where the child is.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A school-age child objects to unfair treatment and understands why some things are forbidden. Objection with respectful words is a skill that adults support even when the answer stays no.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child hears a parent's assurance or pledge and treats a broken promise as a serious hurt. Adults who keep promises, or explain honestly when they cannot, build trust.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A school-age child declares I am going to practise every day, sharing a goal. Small, specific plans are more likely to succeed than large vague declarations.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A school-age child sits with a lonely classmate or stands up for a friend, showing care and solidarity. Adults praise these actions and also teach how to involve an adult when the situation is unsafe.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child at a sleepover or camp may feel homesickness and longing for family. Talking, a comfort item and a planned call help, and missing someone shows healthy attachment.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
